content: 1. The immune response to the dengue vaccine may be reduced in patients receiving immunosuppressive therapies. Close monitoring is required, especially when using infliximab or denosumab. Caution is advised in patients with impaired immune systems or those on concomitant immunosuppressants due to an increased risk of serious infections. 2. Infliximab decreases the efficacy of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 3. Infliximab reduces the effects of diphtheria, tetanus toxoids, acellular pertussis, and inactivated poliovirus vaccines via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants heighten the risk of infection with live vaccines. 4. Infliximab diminishes the efficacy of hepatitis A, hepatitis B, and hepatitis A/typhoid vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated. Immunosuppressants further increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 5. Infliximab reduces the effects of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine (nonavalent) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Immunosuppressive therapies, including corticosteroids, cytotoxic drugs, and radiation, may reduce vaccine immune responses. 6. Infliximab decreases the efficacy of influenza virus vaccines (quadrivalent, trivalent, adjuvanted, recombinant, and intranasal) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 7. Infliximab reduces the effects of the Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 8. Infliximab and leflunomide both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Infliximab and ocrelizumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of ocrelizumab with immunomodulators is expected to heighten the risk of immunosuppression. 10. Infliximab decreases the efficacy of the rabies vaccine (including chick embryo cell-derived formulations) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated. Immunosuppressants may interfere with the development of active immunity. 11. Infliximab reduces the effects of pneumococcal vaccines (13-valent and polyvalent) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 12. Infliximab and mercaptopurine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Infliximab and mycophenolate both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Infliximab and ozanimod both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immunosuppressive therapies may lead to additive immune effects during therapy and in the weeks following administration. 15. Infliximab and pretomanid both increase toxicity risks. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity; avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements. 16. Infliximab and pexidartinib both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents. 17. Infliximab and etanercept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Infliximab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Infliximab and idelalisib both increase immunosuppressive effects, heightening the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Infliximab and fingolimod both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Infliximab and glatiramer both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Infliximab and golimumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Infliximab and lomustine both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Infliximab and murine monoclonal antibodies (e.g., muromonab-CD3) both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Infliximab and lisocabtagene maraleucel both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Infliximab and olaparib both increase pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially prolonging myelosuppressive toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Infliximab and ponesimod both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Infliximab and rabies vaccine interactions may interfere with the development of active immunity. These interactions are contraindicated. 29. Infliximab and meningococcal vaccines (ACYW-135 polysaccharide and group B) interactions reduce vaccine efficacy via pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated. 30. Infliximab and measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccines (live) interactions reduce vaccine efficacy via pharmacodynamic antagonism. These interactions are contraindicated.
